newsitem.title: USA: US Order eyes profitability in 1997.
newsitem.headline: US Order eyes profitability in 1997.

text.p: US Order Inc, a growing player in electronic commerce that went public with an initial public offering (IPO) in June 1995, expects to breakeven in May 1997 and turn a profit for the year, executive vice president Joseph Smith said in an interview on Thursday.
Earlier on Thursday, Herndon, Va-based US Order announced the acquisition of Toldeo, Ohio-based Braun, Simmons & Co for $7 million in cash and stock.
Still pending is US Order's merger with Colonial Data Technologies Corp in a stock deal that will result in the formation of a new company.
Smith did not make any specific earnings projections. But he said revenue is likely to rise to $20 million in 1997 and accelerate rapidly to $100 million by the year 2000.

US Order develops products for online banking and sells and services interactive devices including "smart" telephones. For smaller banks its product offerings include a turnkey solution that permits banks to offer a complete home banking package that focuses on opportunities to extend relationships between the bank and its customers.
Braun, Simmons is a software engineering firm that has bill payment products. Douglas Braun, president of Braun, Simmons, will become chief technology officer of a division within US Order.
Asked how the two companies got involved in the merger, Braun said executives have known each other for some time and their visions of the future were "exactly the same."
Braun said home banking is on the verge of rapid growth as new devices such as smart telephones and high definition interactive television about to offer consumers more alternatives.

US Order was profitable in 1994 when it was a private company, but reported a loss of $4.7 million in 1995 on revenues of $4.2 million. Revenue in 1995 was three times that in 1994. The company has reported losses in the first and second quarters of 1996.
US Order also said on Thursday that it expects to write off nearly $5 million in in-process research and development charges in the third quarter.
The company is still flush with cash from its IPO and its balance sheet shows $50 million in cash and no debt.

In a research report in January 1996 analyst Gary Craft of Friedman, Billings, Ramsey & Co said a key to US Order's growth was alliances with the Visa bankcard organization and Colonial Data. Colonial Data has product and service agreements with six of the regional telephone companies.

In a further report after announcement of the US Order merger with Colonial Data, Craft said the combination was an interesting blend of hardware, content and distribution and could fit in well with a coming convergence of banking and telecommunications. US Order closed down one at 10, while Colonial Data fell 1/2 to 10-1/4.
